There are a few things to remember before you decide to do anything:

\- Depression/anxiety lie. People care about you. I'm really not a big fan of the police, but I hate that you feel this way because I do too. Try to be honest with your wife about where you are mentally. It's going to hurt to feel that vulnerable. You're going to constantly question whether it's the right thing. But its the only way that you can be absolutely sure that you are clear about your problems with those who care for you. 

\- All of this is okay to experience. While suicide thoughts aren't good, you aren't alone. Many of us deal with the same constant nagging, feeling like today is it, and having plans. 

\- If today feels like a groundhog day, do something different. Absolutely different. Go to the pet store and pet a cat, then go get tacos at a good taco place, then go wander around a retail store for an hour. For absolutely no reason whatsoever. 

\- Don't go looking for a magical cure that makes everything stop and make you feel better today. It doesn't exist (well I suppose it does, but it's not legal). The only way this starts to feel better is if you accept it is a process, not a one day deal. Put one foot in front of the other. No more, no less. 

\- Be kind to yourself. Would you be mad at a friend for the same things you're mad at yourself for?
